title: Battle of Poltava
summary: Russian forces under Peter I defeated Charles XII's Swedish army near Poltava in Ukraine in July 1709, during the Great Northern War. Sweden lost its standing as a major power, and the battle marked the start of Russian supremacy in eastern Europe. Charles escaped south into Ottoman territory with about 1,500 followers.

uncertainty.note: Britannica gives 27 June (Old Style) / 8 July (New Style); Encyclopedia of Ukraine gives 8 July.

where.modern_name: Poltava, Ukraine (city centre used as proxy; the fighting was north and west of the city)
where.historical_name: Poltava, Cossack Hetmanate under Muscovite (Russian) suzerainty

importance.justification: Decisive battle of the Great Northern War that ended Sweden's great-power status.
